analysis.investment_thesis: Active Infra is a recently-listed micro-cap infrastructure contractor trading at 26x earnings and ~2.3x book, with a suspicious revenue jump from ₹1 Cr (2022) to ₹89 Cr (2023) and a large 2025 equity raise (₹63 Cr financing inflow) — hallmarks of a speculative IPO lacking the multi-year earnings record I require. With no margin of safety and failing the Graham Number test (price ₹170 vs calculated ~₹117), this is speculation, not investment.
key_strengths: Borrowings reduced from ₹109 Cr (2022) to ₹60 Cr (2025); D/E now ~0.52
Operating CF positive in 3 of last 4 years; ROCE 15.5%
High promoter holding (72.38%) aligns management interest
key_risks: P/E 26 and P/B ~2.3 — no margin of safety; fails Graham Number (₹170 > ₹117)
Revenue explosion from ₹1 Cr to ₹89 Cr in one year suggests reverse-merger/restructuring — no genuine track record
Cyclical civil-construction business with lumpy earnings (Net profit ₹10→9→13 Cr) and FCF collapsing to ₹2 Cr in 2025
red_flags: Recent ₹63 Cr equity raise — insiders/bankers sold at premium pricing
OCF collapsed from ₹32 Cr (2024) to ₹5 Cr (2025) despite revenue being flat — working-capital red flag
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From a strict Graham lens, this security fails nearly every quantitative filter. The P/E of 26 is nearly double my 15x ceiling, and P/B of ~2.3x (market cap ₹267 Cr vs equity ₹116 Cr) exceeds my 1.5x limit. The Graham Number — sqrt(22.5 × EPS ~8.3 × BVPS ~74) ≈ ₹117 — sits 31% below the current ₹170 price, so there is no margin of safety; I am being asked to pay a premium for a speculative growth assumption. The revenue jump from ₹1 Cr to ₹89 Cr between 2022 and 2023 is not organic growth — it signals a corporate restructuring or reverse-listing, which means the "earnings history" is effectively only two reliable years. I require five.

The 2025 financing inflow of ₹63 Cr combined with equity leaping from ₹27 Cr to ₹116 Cr confirms a fresh capital raise — the classic scenario where the seller knows more than the buyer. Construction contracting is inherently cyclical, working-capital intensive (OCF collapsed from ₹32 Cr to ₹5 Cr on flat revenue), and offers no durable economics. While debt reduction and a 72% promoter stake are mildly reassuring, none of this compensates for paying 26x earnings for an unproven, lumpy micro-cap with no dividend record. Mr. Market is offering exuberance here, not a bargain. Avoid.
